clue.text: Endless praise by Tory over independent's refusal to return donation

parts.note: con is the standard short form of Conservative, the Tory party

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a tribute is an expression of praise
I is the usual abbreviation for an independent candidate

indicators.note: returning means the word for refusal is read backwards

parts.note: no is a refusal

explanation.surface: A Conservative rejects a donation while heaping praise on an independent politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' trims TRIBUTE to TRIBUT, and 'to return' turns NO into ON at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A contribution is a gift of money or goods to a cause, the same as a donation.

clue.text: Roughly two points bound to generate criticism

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about or roughly
E and N are two points of the compass, east and north
bound in the sense of certain, as in bound to happen

explanation.surface: Being roughly two points short is certain to draw criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Censure is formal disapproval or harsh criticism.

clue.text: Overlook man's right leg broken by shocking treatment

parts.note: the right-hand letter of man is its last one, N

indicators.note: a broken leg is rearranged, signalling a scramble of its letters

parts.note: ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, treatment by electric shock

explanation.surface: Someone ignores a man's broken right leg while he undergoes electric shock therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man's right' means the rightmost letter of man; 'broken' rearranges LEG to EGL.
explanation.definitionFit: To neglect something is to fail to attend to it, which is to overlook it.

clue.text: Bad mood starting to lessen after short break to move about

indicators.note: short means the synonym loses its final letter

parts.note: a rest is a break
a huff is a fit of sulking, a bad mood

indicators.note: only the start of lessen is used, its opening pair of letters

explanation.surface: A sulk begins to lift after a brief rest, so it is time to get moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts REST to RES; 'starting to' takes just the opening LE of lessen, a loose use the blogger also queried.
explanation.definitionFit: A reshuffle rearranges things, especially posts in a cabinet, moving them about.

clue.text: Well done to be bold with ring for sweetheart

indicators.note: one letter is swapped in place of another, the ring standing for the sweetheart

parts.note: brave as a verb, to face boldly
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Praise for someone bold enough to swap a ring for a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravo is an exclamation of applause, saying well done.

clue.text: He betrays a propensity for going topless

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic tendency or propensity

indicators.note: topless means the first letter of the word for is dropped

explanation.surface: A man who betrays others has a tendency to strip off.
explanation.definitionFit: A traitor is a person who betrays a country, cause or friend.

clue.text: Focus of developments in particle theory

indicators.note: the focus is the centre, so the middle pair of letters is taken

parts.note: an ion is a charged particle

explanation.surface: The central thread of progress in particle physics theory.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a view or belief held, much as a theory is.

clue.text: Crippling fear lest barn can be used by others

indicators.note: crippling something damages it out of shape, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A paralysing fear that a barn will be taken over by other people.
explanation.definitionFit: Something transferable can be handed on, so others can use it.

clue.text: Breaks one's promise concerning information about drugs

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: about signals turning the word round

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
E is ecstasy, so ES is a plural of drugs

explanation.surface: Someone goes back on their word about giving out details on drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To renege is to go back on a promise or commitment.

clue.text: A Republican overcome by a weakness for wanting too much

indicators.note: overcome means covered or engulfed, so the first pair goes inside the next pieces

parts.note: a vice is a moral weakness

explanation.surface: A Republican politician is brought down by a weak spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is greed, an excessive desire for wealth.

clue.text: Occasionally England's extremely moderate about open western border

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for England
very means extremely

indicators.note: about means around, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: to soften is to moderate, as a verb

indicators.note: the western edge of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: England's westerly frontier is now and then very gently relaxed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'western border' of open is its leftmost letter O, which SOFTEN goes 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Every so often is an idiom meaning from time to time, now and then.

clue.text: New Avon university rebuilt with European Union input

indicators.note: rebuilt means put together anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A university on the Avon is redeveloped with funding from Brussels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with ... input' adds EU to AVON U before the whole lot is 'rebuilt'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nouveau is French for new, used in English as in nouveau riche.

clue.text: Possibly caught with crocodile skeleton

parts.note: a batsman caught is one example of being out in cricket
a crocodile is a line of schoolchildren walking in pairs

explanation.surface: A crocodile skeleton, perhaps captured, is on display.
explanation.walkthrough: A crocodile is British for children walking two by two; caught is one way to be dismissed in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline, like a skeleton, is the bare framework of a plan or story.

clue.text: Ships get shelter during first signs of forthcoming tornado

indicators.note: during means within, so one piece is placed inside the other
the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side

explanation.surface: Vessels seek shelter as the first warnings of a coming tornado appear.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleet is a group of ships sailing together.

clue.text: Outrageousness of colours worked extremely charmingly

parts.note: a regiment's colours are its flag
ran as in operated or worked a business

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A painter used colour with great charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrancy is glaring offensiveness, the quality of being outrageous.

clue.text: Every other half term at Harrow beginning to produce effects

indicators.note: every other letter means the alternate ones, the second and fourth
the beginning of Harrow is its first letter

explanation.surface: Every second half-term at Harrow School starts to bear fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a famous English boarding school; half term is a mid-term school holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: An aftermath is the consequences following an event, its effects.

clue.text: He benefits from net price I arranged

indicators.note: arranged means set out in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone gains from a net price that has been set.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipient receives something, so he benefits from it.

clue.text: Syndicate reject entering Middle East to go after business

indicators.note: to go after places the following piece after the first

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: entering means going inside the other piece

parts.note: to bin is to throw away or reject

explanation.surface: A cartel rejects moves into the Middle East to pursue trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A combine is a group of businesses joined together, a syndicate.

clue.text: More aggressive offensive that is meeting resistance

parts.note: a push is a military offensive
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A military offensive meets resistance and becomes more forceful.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushier is the comparative of pushy, more forceful or aggressive.

clue.text: Goods vehicle at work

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to go is to work or function, as a machine does

explanation.surface: A goods vehicle in service.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is goods carried by a ship, plane or lorry.

clue.text: Fancy hat goes against the grain

indicators.note: goes against means it is placed beside the next piece

parts.note: a cap is a hat
rice is a grain

explanation.surface: A fancy hat that runs against the grain.
explanation.definitionFit: A caprice is a whim or sudden fancy.

clue.text: Uproar over performance? Read this

parts.note: a riot is an uproar
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: A rowdy show prompts someone to read out a formal warning.
explanation.walkthrough: To read someone the riot act is to reprimand them; the old British Riot Act was read aloud to disperse crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase read the riot act names the document as the thing you read when scolding.

clue.text: Stupefied birds found in garden border

indicators.note: found in means placed inside

parts.note: a bed is a flower border in a garden
emus are large flightless birds

explanation.surface: Flightless birds turn up in a flower bed, leaving onlookers baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Bemused means bewildered or confused, much like stupefied.

clue.text: Evil spirit inside monastery

annotationWithheld.why: Evil spirit inside monastery (5): DEMON is hidden in 'insiDE MONastery', so 'inside' is both the hidden-word indicator and part of the fodder.

clue.text: Further demonstration of disapproval

parts.note: re- as a prefix means again or further
a proof is a demonstration that something is true

explanation.surface: A second display of disapproval.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole reads as a cryptic definition too: a further proof, and a show of disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproof is a rebuke, an expression of disapproval.

clue.text: Largely feel IT is more set up to benefit a few

definitions.text: set up to benefit a few

indicators.note: largely means most of the words are used, the run sits inside them

explanation.surface: People who feel IT is more established serve only a privileged few.
explanation.definitionFit: Elitism is a system or attitude favouring a select group at the expense of the many.

clue.text: Inspire a friend to tour India regularly

indicators.note: touring something means going around it, so it surrounds the next piece

parts.note: mate is a friend

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter, here the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Encourage a friend to travel round India now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: To animate is to bring to life or enliven, to inspire.

clue.text: Ditch me to cut into accommodation costs in belt- tightening exercise

indicators.note: cutting into means going inside the other piece

parts.note: rent is what is paid for accommodation
a trench is a ditch

explanation.surface: Someone told to cut housing costs as part of a belt-tightening drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrenchment is cutting back spending, an economy drive.
